html:
On 22 March 1873 the Spanish parliament abolished slavery in Puerto Rico, freeing about 30,000 enslaved people. They had to keep working for their masters for three more years under contracts.

Enslaved Africans had been brought to the island since the early 1500s, and in the 1800s many more were imported for the sugar and coffee estates of the south and west. Puerto Rican reformers such as Ramon Emeterio Betances had campaigned for years for abolition.

Spain's first republic, newly in power, passed the law. Emancipation Day is a holiday on the island. Slavery lasted longer in Cuba, until 1886, and in Brazil until 1888. African heritage runs deep in the music and food of Puerto Rico.
sum: On 22 March 1873 the Spanish parliament abolished slavery in Puerto Rico, freeing about 30,000 enslaved people. They had to keep working for their masters for three more years under contracts.
